info.name: Instalflow — Super Admin
info.description:
SUPER_ADMIN-scoped API collection for the Instalflow backend-service. Includes every endpoint that lists SUPER_ADMIN in its `requireRole([...])` guard (verified directly against `src/api/routes/*.ts` on 2026-08-18), plus the auth flow needed to obtain an access token. Endpoints that never grant SUPER_ADMIN (e.g. `/admin`, `/company`, `/company-bank-accounts`, `/commissions/payouts/*-approve`, `/financing`) are intentionally excluded — a SUPER_ADMIN token will get a 403 on those.

Auth model: short-lived JWT access token via `Authorization: Bearer`, refresh token in an httpOnly cookie. CSRF is exempt whenever a Bearer token is present (`csrf-middlewares.ts`), so no CSRF token is needed for any request in this collection once you're logged in.

Run "Login" first — its test script stores the access token into the collection variable `accessToken`, which every other request inherits via collection-level Bearer auth.

The "Tenant Management" and "Platform Revenue" folders are new SUPER_ADMIN-only routes added under `/superadmin` on 2026-08-18 — cross-checked against `docs/swagger/superadmin.swagger.yaml`. They give SUPER_ADMIN a tenant directory/profile, a unified per-tenant activity timeline (fanned in from KYC/settlement/approval/payout/contract/login audit sources — there is no single AuditLog table), per-tenant platform revenue vs GMV, and cross-tenant revenue leaderboards for both tenants and products.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Session bootstrap. Login/refresh are public; the rest require a valid access token. `/auth/*` is fully CSRF-exempt.

request.description: Public. Sets an httpOnly `refresh_token` cookie and returns `accessToken` in the body. The test script below stores it into the `accessToken` collection variable.
Public. Reads the refresh token from the `refresh_token` cookie (or an `Authorization: Bearer <refreshToken>` header as a fallback). Returns a new access/refresh token pair.
Any authenticated role. Revokes the current `UserSession` and clears the refresh cookie.
Any authenticated role.

Roles: COMPANY, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Returns a temp password for the new marketer; controller additionally requires `companyId` on the acting user when role === COMPANY (SUPER_ADMIN is not subject to that check).

item.name: Subscription Plans
item.description: `/superadmin/plans` — entirely SUPER_ADMIN-gated at the router level (`superadmin.routes.ts`). Backs `SubscriptionPlan` CRUD consumed by company onboarding/renewal.

request.description: `interval` is a `SubscriptionInterval` enum (e.g. MONTHLY, YEARLY — check `prisma/schema.prisma` for the full set).
Partial update — every field from `CreateSubscriptionPlanSchema` is optional here.

item.name: Ledger Reconciliation
item.description: `/superadmin/ledger/reconciliation/*` — SUPER_ADMIN-only reads over the Redis-cached output of `ledger-reconciliation.worker.ts` (fed by the daily 02:00 `ledger-reconciliation.scheduler.ts` cron). Read-heavy; the only mutation is cache invalidation.

request.description: Returns `cacheStatus: "cold"` if no reconciliation run has populated the cache yet.

query.description: "true" | "false" — filter to accounts with a balance/journal drift
company UUID, or the literal "global" for platform-level accounts

variable.description: internal numeric LedgerAccount id, not the external uuid

request.description: Purges all reconciliation cache keys from Redis. Use right before manually re-triggering a run, to prevent stale reads.

item.name: Merchant Settlements
item.description: `/merchant-settlements` — reads are shared with COMPANY/ADMIN; `retry` and `generate` are SUPER_ADMIN-exclusive because settlement is fully automatic (weekly `merchant-settlement-generation.scheduler.ts`, Monday 06:00) — COMPANY never approves or initiates its own settlement transfer.

request.description: SUPER_ADMIN sees across all companies; COMPANY/ADMIN are scoped server-side to their own company.
Roles: COMPANY, SUPER_ADMIN (not ADMIN). Returns `MerchantSettlementAuditTrail` rows, each tagged with a `SettlementAuditActor` (SYSTEM/SCHEDULER/WORKER/WEBHOOK/USER).
SUPER_ADMIN-only. Operational recovery for a settlement stuck in TRANSFER_FAILED/TRANSFER_REVERSED — not an approval step, since settlement never required one.
SUPER_ADMIN-only manual/backfill trigger. Runs the exact same idempotent generation path the weekly scheduler invokes — safe to call ad hoc.

item.name: Platform Overview
item.description: `GET /superadmin/overview` — single dashboard-summary endpoint tying tenants, platform revenue, and GMV together.

request.description: Tenant counts by plan, all-time and this-month platform revenue, total GMV, active contract count, top 5 tenants by revenue, top 5 products by GMV.

item.name: Tenant Management
item.description: `/superadmin/tenants/*` — tenant directory, single-tenant profile, and the unified per-tenant activity timeline. New SUPER_ADMIN-only routes (added 2026-08-18) fanned in from KYC/settlement/approval/payout/contract/login audit sources — no single AuditLog table backs this yet.

request.description: Paginated company directory — plan, active subscription, product/user counts, platform revenue, and GMV per tenant.
Full tenant profile — subscription history, bank accounts, user counts by role, financing stats, KYC funnel, and revenue snapshot.

query.description: kyc | settlement | approval | payout | contract | login

request.description: Unified, chronologically-sorted feed of everything this tenant's users did: KYC submit/approve/reject, settlement generate/retry/webhook actions, marketer approval requests, commission payout status changes, financing contract lifecycle transitions, and logins. Post-merge pagination (see collection description) — fine for admin-dashboard use, not a strict cross-table cursor.

item.name: Platform Revenue
item.description: `/superadmin/tenants/:companyId/revenue` and `/superadmin/revenue/*` — new SUPER_ADMIN-only routes (added 2026-08-18). `platformRevenue` (what Instalflow earned — onboarding fee + subscription renewals, from the `PLATFORM_REVENUE` ledger account) is always reported separately from `gmv`/`tenantGmv` (money flowing through a tenant's own products) — the two are never summed.

request.description: Itemized platform revenue transactions for this tenant, plus their GMV (totalFinanced/collected/contract counts) and total merchant settlement payouts.
Every tenant ranked by platform revenue (sorted at the DB level on the live LedgerAccount balance), with GMV shown alongside for the current page.

Every product across every tenant, ranked by GMV (total financed value), with tenant name attached and commissions paid shown per product. Cross-tenant version of the existing company-scoped `GET /analytics/products/performance`.

item.name: Catalog - Products
item.description: `/products` — reads open to any authenticated user; writes gated to COMPANY, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. SUPER_ADMIN can act across every company since `companyId` is a query filter, not an implicit scope.

request.description: Public route in the app, but works fine under an authenticated SUPER_ADMIN token too.
Body is a raw JSON array (`BulkProductsSchema = z.array(BulkProductInputSchema)`), not wrapped in an object.
multipart/form-data, field name `images` (see `uploadMultiple("images")` in `multer.middlewares.ts`). Uploads go to Cloudinary via `cloudinary.service.ts`.
`productId` is taken from the URL and merged server-side — don't include it in the body.

item.name: Catalog - Categories
item.description: `/categories` — reads open to any authenticated user; writes gated to COMPANY, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN.

item.name: Catalog - Variants
item.description: `/variants` — every route gated to COMPANY, ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN (`variants.routes.ts` applies the role check collection-wide).

request.description: `productId` is taken from the URL and merged server-side — omit it from the body.
Max 100 variants per call (`BulkCreateVariantsSchema`).
`imageIds` reference existing `ProductImage` records (upload first via the Products > Upload Gallery Images request).

item.name: KYC Oversight
item.description: `/kyc` — SUPER_ADMIN only has the platform-wide applications list (`GET /kyc/applications`); the submit/approve/reject/document-download routes stay with MARKETER/ADMIN/COMPANY as the maker-checker parties.

request.description: Roles: SUPER_ADMIN, ADMIN, COMPANY, MARKETER. Non-SUPER_ADMIN callers are scoped server-side by `companyId`/`marketerId`; SUPER_ADMIN sees across all companies.

item.name: Customer Management
item.description: `/customers` — role-scoped views; SUPER_ADMIN is included on every route in this file.

request.description: Roles: COMPANY, SUPER_ADMIN only. Full Company → Admin/Marketer → Customer tree.
Ongoing `FinancingContract`s for the customer.

item.name: Installments
item.description: `/installments` — three of six routes include SUPER_ADMIN; the customer-only `GET /customer` and `POST /:installmentId/pay` are intentionally excluded here.

request.description: Roles: ADMIN, COMPANY, SUPER_ADMIN (not CUSTOMER — customers use `GET /customer` instead).
Completion percentage for the `FinancingContract`.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: `/notifications` — no role restriction, just `requireAuth`. In-app notification inbox for whichever account is logged in, including SUPER_ADMIN.

item.name: Utility
item.description: Unauthenticated infrastructure routes, mounted directly in `routes/index.ts`.

request.description: Only needed for cookie/session-based clients. Every request in this collection authenticates with `Authorization: Bearer`, which `csrf-middlewares.ts` exempts from CSRF checks entirely.
